      "species": [],
      "n": 158,
      "n_counts": "individual experiments",
      "verbatim": "For the 158 individual experiments, 65.8% showed statistically significant activity at the experiment level (p < 0.05, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 ), with an average sample size of 8.03 animals per treatment arm and 8.39 animals per control arm."

      "species": [],

      "verbatim": "In one report, only 11% preclinical cancer studies submitted to a major biotechnology company withstood in-house replication ( Begley and Ellis, 2012 )."

  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of features of design and outcomes for preclinical efficacy studies of the drug sunitinib.",
  "what_it_found": "The study found poor reporting and inconsistent design practices in preclinical oncology studies, a tendency towards publication bias, and a lack of clear correlation between preclinical effect sizes and known clinical behavior for sunitinib.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "Effect sizes (standardized mean difference [SMD] using Hedges' g) could not be computed for 174 experiments (52%) due to inadequate reporting (e.g., sample size not provided, effect size reported as a median, lack of error bars, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).",
      "topic": "Reporting issues"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Concealment of allocation or blinded outcome assessment was never reported in studies that advanced to meta-analysis.",
      "topic": "Internal validity"
    },
    {
      "quote": "For external validity ( Figure 3C ), malignancies tested in more and diverse experimental systems tended to show less extreme effect sizes (p < 0.001).",
      "topic": "External validity"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Trim and fill analysis suggests an overestimation of effect size of 45% (SMD changed from −1.8 [−2.1, −1.7] to −1.3 [−1.5, −1.0]) across all indications.",
      "topic": "Publication bias"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Though we did not perform a systematic review to estimate clinical effect sizes for sunitinib against various malignancies, a perusal of the clinical literature suggests little relationship between pooled effect sizes and demonstrated clinical activity.",
      "topic": "Preclinical vs clinical"
    },
    {
      "quote": "We were unable to detect a meaningful relationship between preclinical effect sizes and known clinical behavior.",
      "topic": "Predictive value"
    }
  ]
